notes: Built from ep010.ts lines: only CAPITALS added; words identical to say.
persona: You are an energetic, charismatic YouTuber narrating a vertical short video, talking straight to one friend who is riding a falling satellite. Conversational, expressive, urgent and a little mischievous, with natural breaths. Change your speed, pitch, emphasis and rhythm with what is happening: an urgent hook, tension that climbs line by line (a little faster and tighter each time), a big punch at the break-up, a calm smart explanation about heat shields, thrilled storytelling for the true news story, and a warm, friendly call to action. Words in CAPITALS get extra emphasis. Each line starts with a direction in parentheses: follow it, but never read the directions or the bracketed tags aloud. Keep a brisk, punchy pace throughout, about 180 words per minute: no long pauses inside a line.

lines.style: urgent and quick, right in your ear, hit the number hard
lines.tagged: You're riding a DYING space telescope, falling at over TWENTY EIGHT THOUSAND kilometres an hour.
Every SECOND, you fly almost EIGHT kilometres.
That's nearly Mount EVEREST, sideways, every second.
About a hundred and twenty kilometres up, you hit the first AIR.
It can't move away fast ENOUGH, so it PILES up in front of you.

lines.style: punchy, a little smug, like sharing a secret
lines.tagged: SQUEEZED air gets hot. That's the REAL heat, way more than friction.
At six hundred sixty degrees, aluminium MELTS. Your telescope starts to fall APART.
Around seventy eight kilometres up, it breaks into PIECES.

lines.style: calm and clever, a beat of relief
lines.tagged: That's why EVERY astronaut rides home behind a HEAT SHIELD.

lines.style: leaning in, thrilled, this is real news
lines.tagged: This REALLY happened. On November FOURTH, NASA's Swift telescope came down.

lines.style: storytelling, warm, clear on the place: Soo-MAH-truh
lines.tagged: It burned up over SUMATRA, in Indonesia, after almost TWENTY TWO years in space.

lines.style: proud and amazed, clear on the number
lines.tagged: Along the way, it caught over one thousand seven hundred fifty COSMIC explosions.
What should you survive next? The BEST comment becomes the next video.
